name: WLW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Created for the promotion's 10 September 2002 debut card and decided in a three-fall gauntlet match; when the ring went dark and the belts vanished from a ringside casket, the WLW's own administration named Brett Young and The Suicide Kid, one wrestler from each of the two remaining teams, its first champions.

name: WLW Championship
epitaph: Contested across a two-month, sixteen-man tournament that opened with the promotion's own 10 September 2002 debut card, the title was won by “The Flyking” Will Geddings in a Quadruple Threat match on 22 October 2002; the broadcast that crowned him does not survive in this wing's own held record, but the promotion's own 25 October press conference and 13 December Wrestlebowl V broadcast both confirm the win and Geddings' first defense, a Chicago street fight against Brody Thunder, which he won.

name: WLW North American Championship
epitaph: Created for Wrestlebowl V, 13 December 2002, and decided in a falls-count-anywhere match among four men where the winner had to pin all three opponents; “Redemption” Justin Slayne became the first champion by pinning K.C. Hagen, Eric Cooper and Carl Lumski at once after knocking all three off the top rope through a table.

name: Wrestlebowl Championship
epitaph: A traveling championship the WLW's own broadcast traces through four prior editions at other promotions and venues (Pasadena, the Pontiac Silverdome, Australia and New York) before hosting its fifth at Wrestlebowl V, 13 December 2002; Corey Irons won it there from defending champion Joshua Barnes in a three-way elimination match, with help from a masked interloper's cane.
